title.narrative: Media and Information Literacy in and through Media

description.narrative:
Decision 210 EX/14 recognizes that UNESCO within its unique global mandate is best positioned as the leading organization in the field of media and information literacy and demonstrates several comparative strengths. UNESCO will continue to expand its work in this area including through intersectoral programme (IP4) on Media and Information Literacy and Digital Competencies.
People’s increasing dependence on digital technologies has transformed digital spaces, including social media, in privileged platforms for social interaction. This brings with it a twofold reality of benefits and challenges to social life. The opportunities span social learning, creativity, knowledge exchange, democratic participation and intercultural dialogue. Chief among the challenges are the dissemination of hate speech with discriminatory and racist content, declining human rights and gender equality, spiraling mis-and disinformation including conspiracy theories, which negatively impact people’s understanding of the wider world and their own role as engaged citizens.
To address these challenges, UNESCO will continue to develop, update and support the application of standards and recommendations on media and information literacy and digital competencies at local, regional and global levels, with an emphasis on new actions to apply media and information literacy in digital spaces. Ultimately, efforts will seek to provide people with the knowledge, skills, values and competencies needed to become media and information literate and digital citizens.
A key focus will be on media organizations and professionals, including regulatory bodies, while ensuring cooperation with other stakeholders. UNESCO will expand support to media institutions and libraries, in order to strengthen their capacity to articulate editorial or internal media and information literacy policies that will result in new media programmes. This will be achieved by advancing a Global Media Partnership on Media and Information Literacy. UNESCO will also seek partnership with digital communications platforms as principal actors to integrate media and information literacy in digital spaces.
